absent: Absent: concrete numeric values for file type flags and state flag bits beyond their tested presence.
Absent: internal layouts of group, root, set and filesystem node objects referenced by pointers.
Absent: implementations of next child, next descendant and task set fetch helpers.
Absent: operational details of reference counting, identifier allocation and statistics accumulation.
Absent: boot ordering, hierarchy creation and file registration steps.
Absent: error code definitions and signaling paths for permission and allocation failures.
Absent: locking for per CPU update lists and identifier tables.
Absent: lifetime rules for socket group pointers under migration.

findings.text: A control file descriptor includes a label named name together with an opaque word named private and a size limit named max_write_len alongside an option word named flags plus a displacement named file_offset that locates handle storage within the owning state object.

The same descriptor records its owning subsystem pointer named ss alongside a linkage element named node plus a filesystem operations pointer named kf_ops and a lock validation object named lockdep_key used for dependency tracking.

Read behaviour is offered through several distinct callbacks including a sequential renderer named seq_show accompanied by a handshake named open plus a teardown named release alongside integer shortcuts named read_s64 and read_u64.

Iteration uses a trio named seq_stop plus seq_start and seq_next whereas mutation uses integer acceptors named write_s64 and write_u64 alongside a generic byte sink named write plus an event waiter named poll.

A subsystem descriptor provides state lifecycle hooks including a destructor named css_free accompanied by an allocator named css_alloc plus reset and kill hooks named css_killed and css_reset alongside an activator named css_online plus a deactivator named css_offline and a release notifier named css_released.

Statistics reporting uses three hooks including a per CPU flusher named css_rstat_flush accompanied by a local presenter named css_local_stat_show plus an additional presenter named css_extra_stat_show.
Membership change uses a commit named attach accompanied by a permission check named can_attach plus an abort named cancel_attach.
Task lifecycle uses a hierarchy hook named bind accompanied by termination hooks named release and exit plus creation hooks named fork and cancel_fork and can_fork.
Three single bit options record threaded subtree support named threaded plus early setup named early_init and transparent default hierarchy enablement named implicit_on_dfl.

Identity comprises an identifier allocator named css_idr accompanied by a hierarchy root pointer named root plus a compatibility label named legacy_name alongside a primary label named name and a numeric slot named id.

File registration uses a list head named cfts accompanied by default and legacy table pointers named legacy_cftypes and dfl_cftypes plus a dependency mask named depends_on alongside a statistics lock named rstat_ss_lock and a per CPU update list named lhead.
A peak tracker pairs a linkage element named list with an unsigned measurement named value.

Socket association in the enabled configuration holds optional classification fields named prioidx and classid accompanied by a group pointer named cgroup whereas the disabled configuration defines an empty record with no members.
A task walker records boundary and position cursors for ordinary sets named cset_head and cset_pos accompanied by behaviour bits named flags plus its target subsystem named ss.
The same walker adds threaded set cursors named tcset_head and tcset_pos plus a task cursor named task_pos alongside a current list head named cur_tasks_head.
Current location is retained as set pointers named cur_dcset and cur_cset plus a task pointer named cur_task alongside a registration node named iters_node.
A migration context bundles destination and source group pointers named dst_dcgrp and src_dcgrp with a moving task pointer named task.
Weight parameters are fixed numeric facts with minimum one and default one hundred and maximum ten thousand.
In the configuration without controllers the subsystem count fact is zero and the presence predicate fact is true exactly when that count exceeds zero.

Task iteration option bits are fixed facts with internal marker CSS_TASK_ITER_SKIPPED on bit sixteen whereas inclusion CSS_TASK_ITER_WITH_DEAD uses the third low bit and coverage CSS_TASK_ITER_THREADED uses the second low bit and leaders CSS_TASK_ITER_PROCS uses the lowest bit.
Lifetime notifications distinguish a value called CGROUP_LIFETIME_OFFLINE from a value called CGROUP_LIFETIME_ONLINE.
Migration notifications distinguish a cancellation value called CGROUP_TASK_MIGRATE_CANCELED from a completion value called CGROUP_TASK_MIGRATED and a start value called CGROUP_TASK_MIGRATING.
Subsystem declaration helpers expose either an external controller object or a pair of enablement keys for default and general cases while companion predicates report likely enablement.

Control file tables end with an entry whose label length is zero and small write limits are promoted to a page minus one while a nonzero displacement causes the framework to store the created handle for use only while the owning state stays reachable.

Sequential display requires either the full trio of start and next and stop operations or none of them while a generic byte sink when present supersedes integer acceptors and integer shortcuts exist as conveniences for single number exchange.

Utility controllers marked implicit stay hidden from user visible enablement files yet act enabled everywhere on the default hierarchy and ignore the internal process restriction while tolerating coexistence of stale offline states after hierarchy theft.

Threaded support allows a subtree to disregard process granularity and internal process restrictions whereas implicit marking without threaded marking is unsupported and dependency masks cause silent co enablement until explicit user action.
Numeric identity and textual labels plus hierarchy linkage are established automatically during startup rather than by static initializers.
When threadgroup protection is active, change regions acquire a global percpu read guard accompanied conditionally by a per signal read guard and release them in reverse order.
When controllers are absent, threadgroup change regions impose only a sleepability annotation on entry and no action on exit.
Hierarchy mutation exclusion is provided by a single mutex with paired lock and unlock helpers that become no operation shims when controllers are absent.
Live child and descendant walks require the hierarchy mutex to be held and silently skip dead members while subsystem pointer fetch validates that same mutex protection.
Task association fetch is permitted under scheduler read protection or hierarchy mutex or set lock or when the target is exiting, with a permissive fallback that omits validation.
Parental linkage is derived from the state parent link with absence at the root while descendant testing requires shared hierarchy plus sufficient depth plus ancestor table equality.
Indexed ancestor fetch returns absence for out of range levels and otherwise consults a per group ancestor table while lowest shared ancestor discovery scans downward from the shallower depth.
State liveness is tracked by flag bits where a dying marker and an online marker are tested independently and group death is defined as absence of the online marker.
Selfhood holds when a state pointer equals its group embedded state with an expectation of no subsystem linkage while population is observed through once read counters for sets and children.
Reference management forwards group acquisition and release to embedded state operations with a trial acquisition variant reporting success.
Reference helpers use an inline attribute macro plus an export annotation macro to control linkage.
Task to state resolution proceeds from set fetch to indexed subsystem lookup while group views derive from that state or directly from the default group slot.

Root membership is decided by equality against the initial set entry and hierarchy containment is decided by descendant testing on the default group with an unconditional true answer when controllers are absent.
A safe acquisition helper repeatedly fetches the current state under read protection until a trial hold succeeds, deliberately avoiding an online only variant to support exiting tasks.
Open file and sequence contexts recover their type and state via private pointers stored in the underlying nodes.
Identity and naming services delegate to the backing filesystem node for numeric id and inode plus textual name and path with continuous print variants, collapsing to constant one when disabled.

Early boot sets a migration block flag on the creator thread to keep descendants in the root until ready, and a companion helper clears that flag after initialization with affinity guidance left to the creator.
When controllers are absent, attachment succeeds trivially while statistics construction fails with an invalid argument signal and lifecycle hooks for fork and exit and release do nothing.
Absent controller initialization reports success without action and parental lookup yields absence while pressure indication is negative and path resolution from id is empty.
Disabled accounting shims discard processor time and field inputs without effect.
Enabled accounting credits a legacy per task counter then, unless the task sits in the root, also credits the default hierarchy accumulator for both plain and indexed variants.
Socket classification reads use single access semantics with a fallback of one for priority when the feature is unavailable while writes use single store semantics.
Socket to group resolution simply returns the stored group pointer.
Child and descendant traversals repeatedly invoke a next child or next descendant helper starting from absence until exhaustion for both preorder and postorder.
Task set walks repeatedly fetch first then next elements with destination state output while a leader variant additionally skips members that are not their own group leader.
Subsystem state progresses through allocation then activation with later deactivation and release notification before destruction, plus auxiliary reset and kill signals.
Task movement is signaled as migrating then either migrated or migrate canceled while group lifetime is signaled as online then offline.
Initialization and attachment routines serve as external entry hooks with trivial success behaviour when controllers are absent.
A stored file handle must not outlive its owning state reachability and safe acquisition may spin until a hold succeeds, requiring read protection throughout.
Live walks without hierarchy exclusion risk inconsistent dead skipping and hierarchy theft requires tolerance of lingering offline states.
A header guard macro ensures single inclusion of the control group interface.
